geos.label: South Bay
geos.blurb: San Jose, Saratoga, Sunnyvale, Mountain View

events.title: Dune: Part Three in IMAX
events.note: On the Tech Interactive's dome screen rather than a multiplex, $20. Denis Villeneuve's third, and the dome is the nearest thing to the format he shot for.

events.title: Japanese Tea Garden Free Admission Hour
events.venue: Japanese Tea Garden, Golden Gate Park
events.note: Nine to ten, Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays, the 1894 garden is free to everyone; San Francisco residents are always free with ID. An hour is enough and the hour before opening is the quiet one.

events.title: Rafiki Community Market
events.note: The Bayview health non-profit's free community market — produce and goods, no cost, Monday afternoon.

events.title: Bad Art Mask-querade
events.note: Bad Art Club's mask-making night — sliding scale, nobody turned away. The premise is that you make something deliberately terrible, which is a better unlock than most art workshops manage.

events.title: Bay Area Immersive Theater Makers Gathering: Performer Perspectives
events.note: The people who make immersive theatre in this city talking about performing in it. Free with RSVP; the niche is small and this is where it meets.

events.title: Free Palestinian Folk Dance and Mutual Aid Workshop
events.note: Dabke taught alongside a mutual-aid workshop, free, with the location given on RSVP. Free for Indigenous people of Turtle Island and to anyone with a cost barrier on request.

events.title: NAZA
events.note: Documentary assembled from night-time rooftop conversations in Tel Aviv about the machinery behind Israel's mass targeting. Runs all week here and at New People.

events.title: Lady
events.note: Off-beat comedy about a narcissistic aristocrat who traps an opportunistic director into filming her life. The Roxie's longest-running title this week.

events.title: Author Talk: How to Look Away
events.note: Daniel Peña and Sasha Vasilyuk in conversation. Free, no ticket.

events.title: SalsaCrazy Mondays Halloween
events.note: Lessons from 6:30 and then salsa and bachata until late, in costume. $38 for lessons plus dancing, $10 early-bird for the dancing alone from nine. 21+.

events.title: Hayes Valley Comedy Night
events.note: Free with an Eventbrite RSVP, $20–$25 at the door, two-drink minimum. The Function books better comics than a free Monday has any business getting.

events.title: Sound Baths at Grace Cathedral
events.note: Gongs and singing bowls under the nave's stone vault, lying down if you buy the right ticket. The building does most of the work.

events.title: Inner Wave
events.note: Psyched! Fest opens its week here. The LA band play loose, reverb-heavy psych-pop with a bossa undertow; Heathers, The Fazes and Christina's Trip fill out a four-band bill.

events.title: Blu DeTiger
events.note: Bass-forward dance-pop from a player who came up posting basslines online and can genuinely play; her brother Rex DJs. Sold out downstairs.

events.title: Fred Armisen: Comedy for Musicians But Everyone Is Welcome
events.note: First of three sold-out nights. Armisen's drummer's-joke set, which works on people who cannot play as well as on people who can. Sold out.

events.title: Mirthquake
events.note: Monday stand-up in the Richmond with $5 drinks, free with RSVP, 21+. One of several free comedy nights this week and the furthest west.

events.title: The War and Treaty
events.note: Michael and Tanya Trotter sing gospel-soul duets with the volume of a revival meeting, and the Chapel's old sanctuary is the right room for it. Blank Page and Jordan Babbs open.

events.title: Wine Lips
events.note: Psyched! Fest's other Monday booking. The Toronto trio play garage-psych at a sprint — three chords and no pauses. Buddy Wynkoop and Hazy Portraits open. All ages.

events.title: The History of Concrete
events.note: John Wilson's first feature after How To with John Wilson — the same accidental-encounter method at feature length, and much stranger for it.

events.title: Lil Pete: Real Is Back Tour
events.note: Second of two nights for the Fillmore-district rapper, whose melodic street-rap is more popular in this city than its national profile suggests. A hometown run.

events.title: Open Mic Night
events.note: The city's longest-running open mic, in its oldest surviving saloon. Sign-up is early and the room is generous.

events.title: Town Biz Comedy Night
events.note: HellaFunny's free Monday in Temescal, at a new agave bar and Oaxacan kitchen. Free with RSVP; food and drink for purchase.

events.title: Community Mondays: Fil Am Futurism with Karl Evangelista and Grex
events.note: The Freight's $5-suggested Monday series, here given over to guitarist Karl Evangelista and his band Grex — Filipino-American free improvisation with a rock rhythm section. The most adventurous five dollars in the East Bay.

events.title: Laura Anglade
events.note: Brooklyn-based, French-raised jazz singer who works the bossa and Great American Songbook repertoire at conversational volume. $30–$59, which is the cheapest Yoshi's gets this week.

events.title: Beabadoobee
events.note: With Wisp. Arena show, which the brief deprioritises — listed for completeness.

events.title: Bobby McFerrin
events.note: Ten Grammys, one novelty hit everyone remembers, and a body of improvised solo vocal work that almost nobody else attempts. In a 600-seat listening room with the lights up. The booking of the week in the East Bay.

events.title: Sharks vs Sabres
events.note: Buffalo in town on a Tuesday. The Shark Tank is loud for a 17,000-seat building and the cheap seats stay cheap.

events.title: W.A.S.P.
events.note: Blackie Lawless's band on a double bill with KK's Priest — two-thirds of a Judas Priest lineage act. Theatrical 1980s metal played straight. Time not published on the mirror this file uses.

events.title: Transportation and Senior Services Resource Fair
events.note: Ten until noon in the Sequoia Room. Free, civic, and the kind of thing that never reaches a listings site.

events.title: Civic Center Soundtrack
events.note: Free lunchtime concerts and food trucks on Fulton Plaza, Tuesdays and Thursdays, midday to three. The booking is usually a local band and the plaza is genuinely pleasant in October.

events.title: Noe Valley Night Market
events.note: Five to eight in the town square — makers, food, and the neighbourhood out in the street. The square posts its next date only, so it is worth checking rather than assuming a rhythm.

events.title: Found Company: A Spontaneous Staged Reading
events.note: A play read cold by a cast assembled that evening. $20.

events.title: French Thriller Night: Les Algues Vertes
events.note: Pierre Jolivet's film about the green-algae scandal on the Breton coast — an environmental thriller that is really about agricultural lobbying. English subtitles, $10.

events.title: One City One Book: Cities as Ancestors
events.note: The library's citywide reading programme, on what a city inherits from the one before it. Free, Koret Auditorium.

events.title: PBS Film Preview: Crime and Punishment in America
events.note: An early look at Lynn Novick's series, at KQED's Mission Street building. $22.

events.title: When ICE Melts
events.note: Director Kip Hedges in person, with a Q&A moderated by SFSU faculty. Labour-organising documentary; the in-person element is the reason to pick this screening.

events.title: APATure 2026
events.note: Kearny Street Workshop's annual Asian Pacific American arts festival brings its film programme here, curated by Lisa Jarrett, Aaron Oculto, Jocelyn Ng and Noelani Piters. Shorts by nine Bay Area makers.

events.title: Learn About SF's Iconic Tiled Stairways
events.note: A free evening talk on the city's mosaic stairways — the 16th Avenue tiled steps and their imitators. An hour and a half, Glen Park.

events.title: Nightmare at the Knockout
events.note: Billed as a Halloween rock'n'roll tribute fever dream, which is about the level of precision the Knockout offers in advance. Expect four bands and no gaps.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Mischief's hijacking of Peter Pan, in which an am-dram company's flying rig fails in every way a flying rig can. Broad, exactly timed, and the best-engineered farce in the city.

events.title: SF History Night: Pacific Heights
events.note: The historical society's monthly lecture, this time on Pacific Heights. $10, and the slides are always better than the title.

events.title: $1 Margaritas and Disco Taco Tuesday
events.note: No cover, disco records, dollar margaritas in SoMa. Not programming so much as a reliable Tuesday.

events.title: Manon
events.note: Massenet's Manon, late in its run. Five acts of a young woman priced by everyone around her; the score is all surface charm and the staging has to supply the rot.

events.title: Fred Armisen: Comedy for Musicians But Everyone Is Welcome
events.note: Second of three, added by demand. Sold out.

events.title: Slothrust
events.note: Night one of two. Leah Wellbaum's trio play blues-shaped grunge with jazz-school chords underneath — the Dystopian Theatre tour. Um, Jennifer? open. All ages.

events.title: The Wldlfe
events.note: Indianapolis bedroom-pop four-piece with a bright, major-key guitar sound; Landon Conrath and brendon b open. A young-crowd show in a 500-cap room.

events.title: Violet Grohl
events.note: A famous surname attached to a real voice — she sings closer to Alanis Morissette than to her father's band. Suzy Clue opens. The room is 400 capacity and that will not last.

events.title: Wand
events.note: Cory Hanson's band have moved from garage-psych into something closer to Yo La Tengo's long-form guitar drift. The best of the Psyched! Fest bookings in this room.

events.title: jackzebra
events.note: The Zhuang Zhuang tour — Mandarin-language indie rock out of the mainland, booked by Goldenvoice into a 300-cap room. All ages, $42.40, show at eight.

events.title: Filipiñana
events.note: Last night of the FiliKula run. Rafael Manuel's debut feature follows a teenage caddie at a Manila golf club — static, patient, very funny about class.

events.title: Kilowatt Karaoke
events.note: The Mission bar's standing Tuesday. Listed because the DICE calendar carries it as a dated event and because a free Tuesday is worth knowing about.

events.title: The Cottontails and After-Hours Jam
events.note: The Woodchopper's Ball Halloween edition — Western swing and jump blues, then an open jam for anyone who brought an instrument. $20, nine o'clock.

events.title: Rewind Presents: The Craft with Live Drag!
events.note: The 1996 teen-witch film with live drag by Mary Vice over the top. The best-pitched Halloween-week repertory booking in the city: a cult film and a cabaret at once.

events.title: Halloween Portrait Party: Mini Marathon Fundraiser
events.note: Sit for a portrait in costume, pay what you like, and the money goes to the bar's artist grant. Free in, and the sort of thing nothing else in the city does.

events.title: Oh, Mary!
events.note: Cole Escola's Mary Todd Lincoln as a thwarted cabaret singer, at the Curran rather than an A.C.T. house. A.C.T. publishes no curtain times anywhere on its site, which is the theatre's choice and not a fetch failure — check the ticket page.

events.title: Slow Pulp
events.note: First of two nights. Chicago four-piece playing slack, warm guitar-pop with Emily Massey's voice sitting just behind the beat. Snuggle open.

events.title: The Moth SF StorySLAM: Strange Encounters
events.note: Ten names out of a hat, five minutes each, on the theme Strange Encounters. The Moth's open-mic format is better than its radio hour because nobody has been edited.

events.title: Halloween Karaoke Singing Contest
events.note: $300 in cash prizes for singing in costume, free to attend, five until eleven.

events.title: Lenny Pearce: Toddler Rave
events.note: A techno set for small children, which is a real genre now and sells out 2,800-seat rooms. Doors five, show six. Earplugs are provided and needed.

events.title: Becoming Leaderful
events.note: Local organisers on how to build the communities people say they want. Free, ninety minutes.

events.title: Liberation
events.note: Final preview. Bess Wohl's West Coast premiere: a daughter restages her mother's 1970s consciousness-raising group and keeps interrupting it. Whitney White directs, and it goes on to the Geffen in January. berkeleyrep.org answered this run with a redirect loop, so the time comes from a ticketing listing.

events.title: Mezcal & Mole Comedy Night
events.note: The Tuesday half of the same residency. Free with RSVP.

events.title: Direct From Sweden: The Music of ABBA
events.note: A Swedish tribute band doing the catalogue properly, which in ABBA's case means the arrangements matter. Tribute act, so listed and not featured. Also at Montalvo the next night.

events.title: Last Tuesdays Comedy
events.note: Laugh City's monthly, with comics off HBO and Comedy Central, in a downtown Oakland bar. Free with RSVP.

events.title: $6 Drive-In Movie Night
events.note: Six dollars a head on Tuesdays at the West Wind drive-in, children cheaper. The operator's own page draws its showtimes by script, so the title is not confirmable here — the price and the night are.

events.title: Bryson Tiller
events.note: With Majid Jordan, Ty Dolla $ign and Austin Millz, at an outdoor shed in late October — bring a coat. The last big night of Concord's season.

events.title: Havok
events.note: Denver thrash, fast and technical. Found on the regional sweep rather than on Cornerstone's own calendar, which lists nothing between the 25th and 12 November — so treat the time as unconfirmed.

events.title: Direct From Sweden: The Music of ABBA
events.venue: Carriage House Theatre, Montalvo Arts Center
events.note: The same Swedish tribute band that plays Yoshi's the night before, here in Montalvo's 300-seat barn — the better room for it by a distance. Prices sit behind the ticket link and add an $8 fee.

events.title: San Jose Barracuda vs Abbotsford Canucks
events.note: Minor-league hockey in a 4,200-seat room next door to the big one, seven o'clock. Cheap, fast and walkable from Diridon.

events.title: Dracula
events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Half past seven, with a pre-show talk. Steven Dietz's adaptation of Stoker, directed by Giovanna Sardelli with illusions by Jim Steinmeyer — the stage tricks are the point and they are very good. Final week of the run, which closes on 1 November.

events.title: Rea Kapur
events.note: Eight o'clock. A Wednesday headline slot at the Improv, which is where the club takes its risks.

events.title: Unreal Magic with Sean Francisco and Jake Berg
events.note: Close-up magic rather than stand-up, eight o'clock, 21+, two-item minimum. The club's Wednesdays are its oddest bookings and usually its best.

events.title: Foreigner
events.note: The last booking of the Mountain Winery's 2026 hillside season, and a legacy act with one original member. The amphitheatre and the view are the reason to go.

events.title: G-Eazy and Logic
events.note: An outdoor shed at the end of October, which in Mountain View means a cold night under an open roof. Bring layers; the lot is $40.

events.title: Jérémy Charbonnel
events.note: French stand-up in Menlo Park, doors seven, show eight. The Guild books an unusually wide spread and this is the far end of it.

events.title: Japanese Tea Garden Free Admission Hour
events.venue: Japanese Tea Garden, Golden Gate Park
events.note: The Wednesday hour. Free nine to ten; residents always free with ID.

events.title: Free Admission Day at YBCA
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: Galleries free every Wednesday, which is the point of saying so. On view: Dread Scott's The Body Politic, GaHee Park's Behind the Curtain and Rael San Fratello's Prototypes and Provocations.

events.title: Free Art Workshop: Pop-up Mini Haunted House
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: Build a pop-up haunted house in the Grand Lobby, free with registration, on the free day. Two hours, and aimed at anyone who will sit still.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Wednesday matinee. Mischief's hijacking of Peter Pan, in which an am-dram company's flying rig fails in every way a flying rig can. Broad, exactly timed, and the best-engineered farce in the city.

events.title: Free NeuroNight SF
events.note: Brain games and short keynotes from working neuroscientists, free, with a raffle. The kind of thing the brief's oddities column exists for.

events.title: Henry Street Fall Porch Party
events.note: A Duboce Triangle block's mini porch party — bring a treat to share. Ninety minutes, free, and about as neighbourhood as this digest gets.

events.title: Mission Bernal Tasting: Ten Countries in Four Blocks
events.note: A walking tasting down the Mission Street corridor between the Mission and Bernal — ten cuisines in four blocks, which is an accurate description of that stretch. $65.

events.title: Chess Lecture at the Bernal Library
events.note: Free chess instruction in the branch library. Weekly and unglamorous and useful.

events.title: Desierto
events.note: Tenth anniversary of Jonás Cuarón's border thriller, which strips the chase down to survival horror. Harsher now than it was in 2016.

events.title: Made In This Place: Closing Party
events.note: The last night of KALW's multimedia exhibition of Bay Area artists in their own words. Free, two hours, and the station's building is worth seeing.

events.title: Madrone x SFPL: Blind Book Art-Making Challenge
events.note: Pick a gift-wrapped mystery, horror or thriller off the library's table, read the first pages, make art from them. Space is limited and it is free.

events.title: Making Marie Antoinette
events.note: Eleanor Coppola's behind-the-scenes record of her daughter directing the 2006 film. Pairs with the 4K restoration two hours later; see both and the double bill is the point.

events.title: Terror Vault: 1874 Halloween Haunt
events.note: Into The Dark's haunt in the Old Mint's vaults — a real 1874 building with real iron doors, which is why this works where mall haunts do not. Final week.

events.title: Untypical Girl Rock'n'Roll Happy Hour
events.note: Early-evening DJ set of girl-group and garage 45s, named for the Rough Trade compilation. Happy-hour prices.

events.title: Author Talk: Parini Shroff with Tanya Žilinskas
events.note: The Bandit Queens author in conversation. Free.

events.title: Astronomy on Tap SF
events.note: Working astronomers give short talks about their actual research in a nightclub, with a one-drink minimum. Free, and the most reliably interesting weeknight in the Mission.

events.title: Cat Drama, J McKinnon and Sour Pop
events.note: Three local guitar bands on a Wednesday, which is what this room is for. Cat Drama play scrappy, fast power-pop.

events.title: Death By Aria: Haunted Halloween Concert
events.note: Opera arias about dying, sung in the cathedral, with an aerial act overhead. $75 and the most lavishly silly premise of the week.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Wednesday evening. Mischief's hijacking of Peter Pan, in which an am-dram company's flying rig fails in every way a flying rig can. Broad, exactly timed, and the best-engineered farce in the city.

events.title: SF State Rooftop Stargazing
events.note: The university's big telescope on the roof, free and open to the public, two hours, weather permitting — and in October on the west side that caveat is doing real work.

events.title: The Dead Cassettes, Moon Darling and Baystar
events.note: Three Bay Area bands, power-pop to shoegaze, straight after the happy hour.

events.title: Word for Word: Assimilation
events.note: Word for Word stage E.L. Doctorow's Assimilation and Tatyana Tolstaya's story word for word, stage directions included — a green-card marriage that turns real. The company's method is the draw: nothing is adapted away.

events.title: Hobogoblins, Ghost Town Gospel and Asunder Sweet
events.note: Three local bands, free in. Gothic Americana at the raggedy end.

events.title: Aliza Kelly's Haunted Tea Party
events.note: The astrologer's Spooky Season tour, fully seated in a 1931 supper club — a live reading-and-lecture night that belongs squarely in the brief's oddities column. 21+.

events.title: An Evening With Theo Katzman
events.note: The Vulfpeck guitarist solo, which means songs rather than grooves — closer to 1970s Laurel Canyon than to the funk band that pays his bills.

events.title: Freak Slug
events.note: Manchester's Xenya Genovese makes hazy, slightly off-kilter bedroom soul — the Amulet tour. Mamalarky, who write much tighter songs, are the better reason to arrive early.

events.title: Fred Armisen: Comedy for Musicians But Everyone Is Welcome
events.note: Third of three, added by demand. Sold out. Three nights in a 1,400-seat room is the story here.

events.title: Great Lake Swimmers
events.note: Tony Dekker's Ontario band record in churches and silos for the reverb, and this low-ceilinged basement is a deliberate change of scale. Jesse Sykes plays a duo set first.

events.title: Oh, Rocky! Immersive Rocky Horror Club Night
events.note: Good Ships stage Rocky Horror as a club night with drag and tarot readings, in El Rio's back patio and bar. $15, 21+, and the better of the week's two Rocky Horror options because you are in it.

events.title: Pixel Grip
events.note: Chicago darkwave trio with a dominatrix-at-the-mic stage presence; Dark Chisme, Grizz and Blood Rave make it a goth-club night rather than a gig.

events.title: Slothrust
events.note: The second of two nights, same support. Two nights in a 350-cap room by a band that could fill a bigger one is worth noting while this room lasts — it closes at the end of 2026.

events.title: The Moors
events.note: Jen Silverman's gothic comedy about two sisters, a governess and a dog on the Yorkshire moors — a Brontë parody with real teeth. Faculty-and-student production; time confirmed, room small.

events.title: The Wildwoods
events.note: Nebraska folk trio — close family harmony, mostly acoustic — in the Richmond's repertory cinema, which books live music on the nights it is not showing films. $22.

events.title: We Are Scientists
events.note: Twenty-one years on from With Love and Squalor and still a better live band than a recorded one, largely because Keith Murray talks between songs. Soft Contact open. They also play Menlo Park on Sunday.

events.title: Lady
events.note: Second week of the aristocrat comedy. Late show.

events.title: Marie Antoinette (4K Restoration)
events.note: Sofia Coppola's pastel, anachronistic Versailles, restored. Booed at Cannes, vindicated since; the new transfer is the reason to see it in a room.

events.title: Lavay Smith and Her Red Hot Skillet Lickers
events.note: Thirty years of Kansas City jump blues and 1940s swing, played by a band that never left. $15 and the cheapest big-band ticket in the city.

events.title: Top Chefs Potluck: DJ Halloween Party
events.note: Bay Area cooks bring a dish, Bay Area DJs bring records, and nobody charges at the door before 9:30 ($5 after). More community night than club night.

events.title: Ax and the Hatchetmen
events.note: Chicago eight-piece with horns and a frontman who writes like he has read too much Springsteen, which is the right amount. The Rare Occasions support. The Late Checkout tour.

events.title: Scaling Intelligence: Opening Night
events.note: Eleven commissioned works on computing at scale, made with Modal's cloud credits — satellite views next to microbial colonies next to the inside of a neural network. Registration is full; there is a waitlist.

events.title: Slow Pulp
events.note: The second night, no support listed. Two sold nights at the Fillmore is a step up for them.

events.title: Exhibition Tour: Some Particular Heaven
events.note: A quarter-past-noon walk through the collection show on ideas of utopia. Short, free with admission.

events.title: Our Sister Hedy
events.note: Hong Kong Cinema: Rarities and Restorations. Paul Fonoroff introduces this 1957 family dramedy in person, as he does once a year; it is barely ever screened.

events.title: Daley
events.note: The Manchester singer's falsetto soul — one of the genuinely distinctive voices in contemporary R&B and a long way from the arena version of it. Sold out.

events.title: Liberation
events.note: Opening night, eight o'clock. Bess Wohl's West Coast premiere: a daughter restages her mother's 1970s consciousness-raising group and keeps interrupting it. Whitney White directs, and it goes on to the Geffen in January. berkeleyrep.org answered this run with a redirect loop, so the time comes from a ticketing listing.

events.title: Mumiy Troll
events.note: Thirty years of Vladivostok art-rock, and one of the few Russian bands of that generation still touring the West. $60 plus fees. Doors seven.

events.title: Gorillaz
events.note: With Little Simz and Deltron 3030 — and Deltron 3030 is Del the Funky Homosapien and Dan the Automator, which makes this an Oakland homecoming buried on an arena bill. The brief says never feature an arena show; this one argues with that.

events.title: Mdou Moctar
events.note: Tuareg desert blues played at the volume of a rock band, with the guitar tuned for it. One of the best live acts touring anywhere, in a 500-cap San Jose room. Seven o'clock.

events.title: Sharks vs Canucks
events.note: Vancouver, seven o'clock. The old rivalry and usually the better game of the week.

events.title: Psychic Standup with Karen Rontowski
events.note: Stand-up and cold readings in the same set, with Kelly Evans. Half past seven, 21+.

events.title: Chad & JT
events.note: The podcast duo's live show, eight o'clock.

events.title: Caifanes
events.note: The Mexico City band who made rock en español sound like its own tradition rather than an import. Thirty-five years on and still the reference point. The South Bay booking of the week.

events.title: Free Trick-or-Treat Around Historic Aircraft
events.note: Trunk-or-treat under the wings at the Hiller, five until seven, free to attend. A 747 cockpit and a Halloween trail is a better combination than it sounds.

events.title: Blues Traveler
events.note: First of two nights. John Popper's harmonica is still the reason, and a 500-cap room is a long way down from where they played in 1995. The Last Revel open.

events.title: SF Symphony Open Rehearsal: Elim Chan
events.note: The Thursday morning open rehearsal for the same programme. Cheaper than the concert, and you hear Chan talk to the orchestra, which is the interesting part.

events.title: Civic Center Soundtrack
events.note: The Thursday lunchtime concert on Fulton Plaza. Free, midday to three, food trucks.

events.title: Día de los Muertos and Halloween at Mission Community Market
events.note: The Bartlett Street market marks both at once, free, three until seven. Ofrenda, produce and a lot of children in costume.

events.title: NAZA
events.note: Matinee. See Monday's note — the Tel Aviv rooftop documentary.

events.title: Trick or Treating at the Ferry Building
events.note: The Ferry Building's merchants hand out sweets, five to seven, free. Indoors if it rains, which in October it will not.

events.title: Urban Wildlife in Textile: Free Art Opening
events.note: Opening night for a textile show about the animals that live in cities. Free.

events.title: Echoes of the Past: Nature as Metaphor
events.note: Opening night in the Grant Avenue storefront gallery. Free.

events.title: Halloween Screening: Zombie Films
events.note: German cinema invented a good deal of screen horror and the Goethe-Institut is showing the zombie end of it, free and open to the public.

events.title: Making Marie Antoinette
events.note: Second screening of the Coppola-on-Coppola documentary.

events.title: New People: The Great Experiment
events.note: At New People Cinema in Japantown, with a post-screening Q&A with co-director Eric. Documentary.

events.title: Practical Magic 2 Outdoor Movie Night
events.note: The sequel, projected on the scoreboard with the field open. $28 all in, fees included, and a ballpark is a very good place to watch a witch film.

events.title: Season of the Witch: Halloween Horror Art Print Show
events.note: The Poster Institute takes Kilowatt's upstairs for a horror print show — screenprints on the wall and for sale, free to walk in. Runs the evening.

events.title: Substance Festival San Francisco Day 3
events.note: The festival's third day moves off Polk Street to an afterparty venue. $30. The Great American Music Hall bills are the main stage; this is the late end.

events.title: Terror Vault: 1874 Halloween Haunt
events.note: Final-week Thursday in the Old Mint's vaults.

events.title: The Art Remains Closing Reception
events.note: Closing reception, free. SOMArts' Brannan Street hall is one of the last big artist-run spaces downtown.

events.title: Woman in the Dunes
events.note: Hiroshi Teshigahara's 1964 film of a man trapped in a sand pit by a village — one of the great art-house sensations of its decade and still physically unpleasant in the right way.

events.title: Desire and MOTHERMARY
events.note: Night one of Substance Festival, the Bay's darkwave and post-punk gathering. Desire's Italo-disco melancholy headlines over Sacred Skin, Madeline Goldstein, clubdrugs and Violet Thrones — five acts from 6:30.

events.title: Flight Club: Adult Flight Night
events.note: The Presidio trampoline park, 18-plus, for two hours. $20 an hour. Filed under oddities with no apology.

events.title: Halloween Cover Show
events.note: Spencer Noble, The Band Yo!, Bromf and Mitch Rocket each play someone else's set. Downstairs, under the print show.

events.title: ODC/Dance presents: Unplugged
events.note: The company's informal showing — work in progress, talked through by the choreographers rather than presented finished. The most useful dance ticket of the week for anyone who wants to see how it is made.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Mischief's hijacking of Peter Pan, in which an am-dram company's flying rig fails in every way a flying rig can. Broad, exactly timed, and the best-engineered farce in the city.

events.title: SF Latino Film Festival: Bird of 400 Voices
events.note: The 18th Cine+Más festival, with a live performance alongside the screening. Films free to $15 across the festival; this one is ticketed.

events.title: Word for Word: Assimilation
events.note: Word for Word stage E.L. Doctorow's Assimilation and Tatyana Tolstaya's story word for word, stage directions included — a green-card marriage that turns real. The company's method is the draw: nothing is adapted away.

events.title: SF Symphony: Elim Chan conducts Adams, Mendelssohn and Brahms
events.note: Brahms's Nänie with the Symphony Chorus, Pärt's Magnificat and Adams's Doctor Atomic Symphony — both firsts for this orchestra — around Renaud Capuçon in the Mendelssohn concerto. Elim Chan conducts. The programme of the week.

events.title: Daði Freyr
events.note: The Icelandic synth-pop oddity who went viral on a Eurovision entry and turned out to have a catalogue. BRÍET, also Icelandic and much more soulful, opens. The Too Much, Not Enough tour.

events.title: Drunk Theatre: Nightmare on Valencia St.
events.note: A comedian takes five shots and then has to keep up with the scene. The Halloween special, in the Valencia Street black box.

events.title: Francis of Delirium
events.note: Jana Bahrich's Luxembourg-based project — grunge-scaled guitars under a voice that stays conversational. swell foop open.

events.title: Hayden Everett and Jackson Lundy
events.note: Two songwriters on a co-headline, country-leaning and unamplified in places. All ages, $28.08, eight o'clock.

events.title: Katie Pruitt
events.note: Nashville songwriter whose subject is leaving the church she grew up in; the Fools for the Fleeting tour. Olivia Barton opens. One of the better-value tickets of the week.

events.title: Lady
events.note: Evening show.

events.title: Lady Camden Presents: The Peach Pit Cabaret
events.note: Drag cabaret from the San Francisco-raised, ballet-trained Lady Camden, with Willow Pill and guests. The room's velvet-and-mirrors decor does most of the staging for them. 21+.

events.title: Patrick Wolf
events.note: The English songwriter's first touring in years, back to the harp-and-viola chamber-pop of his early records rather than the glam of the middle ones. Abhora opens.

events.title: The First Annual Dracula Party
events.note: Self-explanatory and first of its kind. The Knockout's Halloween programming is the most committed in the city and this is its opening night.

events.title: A Pre-Halloween Bash
events.note: Three tributes and a belly-dance troupe: Astrozombies SF do the Misfits, Rusty Chains do Soundgarden and Alice in Chains, Caution do Operation Ivy with members of Omnigone. Costume contest. 21+.

events.title: New People: Hausu
events.note: Nobuhiko Obayashi's 1977 haunted-house film, which looks like a cat food advert having a breakdown. Possibly the correct Halloween booking in the city and certainly the most unhinged.

events.title: Crazy Karaoke
events.note: New Thursday karaoke night with $3 shots, free with RSVP, 21+, until close.

events.title: The Blair Witch Project
events.note: The found-footage film that made the form, on the Thursday before Halloween. Twenty-seven years on, the camping-in-the-dark half still works and the exposition does not.

events.title: The Tubs
events.note: Welsh guitar band carrying the Go-Betweens and early Fairport jangle into something harder-edged; Owen Williams writes about grief without flinching. Touch Girl Apple Blossom and Dusty Slims open.

events.title: Supernova — Open to Close
events.note: One DJ, all night, doors at 10. The Foundry's open-to-close format is the closest thing the city has to a proper Berlin booking.

events.title: Discoween
events.note: DJs Maryzelle, Scam Jones, Nicky D. and Ochenta, late. Disco, not house.

events.title: Dilated Peoples
events.note: Evidence, Rakaa and DJ Babu, intact. Twenty-five years of West Coast boom-bap played by people who still cut records on turntables. Coyote supports. The best hip-hop booking of the week.

events.title: Inference as Instrument
events.note: The day-after panel: Iana Chugunova, Ryan Phillips of Runway and Charles Frye of Modal on what these tools do to authorship. Gray Area is the only room in the file that books this subject seriously.

events.title: Madrone Presents Fillmore Sessions
events.note: The bar's own live-music night, booked out of the neighbourhood rather than off a tour routing. Free.

events.title: Nile
events.note: Thirty years of Egyptology-themed technical death metal. An odd booking for a Minna Street club and all the better for it.

events.title: Oh, Mary!
events.note: Cole Escola's Mary Todd Lincoln as a thwarted cabaret singer, at the Curran rather than an A.C.T. house. A.C.T. publishes no curtain times anywhere on its site, which is the theatre's choice and not a fetch failure — check the ticket page.

events.title: Rossi.
events.note: The British DJ's ravey, breakbeat-driven house on 1015's main floor. 21+.

events.title: Shake & Pop
events.note: Late Thursday DJ night, soul and 60s pop 45s. Free.

events.title: Swedm and Nation
events.note: Bass and dubstep on the Great Northern's main floor. 21+.

events.title: The Chicks
events.note: First of two nights. Twenty-three years since they were run off country radio for saying the obvious, and the harmonies are still the point. A 3,300-seat room, not an arena.

events.title: The Haunt
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: Bat Witch Ghost take over the Forum for three nights: part netherworld labyrinth, part laser-lit speakeasy, entirely built by artists. $25, members $15, under-12s free. The best-made Halloween thing in the city that is not a nightclub.

events.title: bleood
events.note: Rage-adjacent internet rap in a 1,400-cap ballroom. No support listed and no start time published on the mirror this file uses.

events.title: Halloween Trick-or-Treating in the North Shattuck District
events.note: Shopfronts along North Shattuck, three until six, alongside the Thursday farmers' market. Free, all ages.

events.title: Outdoor Silent Disco
events.note: A hundred and fifty free headsets and costume prizes in a Broadway lot, five until half past seven. Last one of the season, RSVP required.

events.title: Concision, State of Reliance, Let Them Eat Horses and Damnata
events.note: Four bands for five dollars at the volunteer-run all-ages club, half past six. Happydays presents; grindcore and screamo end of the hardcore spectrum.

events.title: Celluloid Frontiers: A Missing Can of Film and Stop Genocide
events.note: Two documentaries on what gets recorded and what gets lost, in the Celluloid Frontiers series. Seven o'clock.

events.title: Newberry & Verch
events.note: Joe Newberry and April Verch — clawhammer banjo and Ottawa Valley fiddle, both of them step-dancers as well. $25 in a 50-seat Berkeley listening room, which is the correct scale for this music.

events.title: POC Comedy Night
events.note: HellaFunny's new Thursday showcase in Temescal, free with RSVP.

events.title: Bridge City Sinners
events.note: Portland's dark-folk string band, played at punk speed with a washtub bass. Liam St. John and Shawn D'Amario open. $25 plus fees, half past seven.

events.title: Grace Kelly
events.note: Saxophonist, singer and arranger who came up as a prodigy and has spent the years since refusing to stay in the straight-ahead lane. $39–$79.

events.title: Theatre des Vampires: The Vampire Lestat
events.note: A drag show of Anne Rice's Lestat with live music from Pretty Frankenstein. $12–$15, 21+, sold out. Exactly the kind of thing this room exists for.

events.title: Coco & Breezy
events.note: The twin-sister DJ duo's melodic house, in a Shattuck Avenue beer hall. Also off the sweep; not on the venue's own page.

events.title: Ernest Aines
events.note: In Bernard Maybeck's 1910 church, which is the reason to go whatever is played. Second of the artist's three Bay Area church dates this week.

events.title: Liberation
events.note: Second night of the run proper. Curtain time unconfirmed — the theatre's own site could not be read this run.

events.title: Bluey's Big Play
events.venue: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Broadway San Jose's half-term booking: the Heelers as puppets, with a Joff Bush score played live. Six o'clock, and the only thing in the digest aimed squarely at four-year-olds.

events.title: Dracula
events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Steven Dietz's adaptation of Stoker, directed by Giovanna Sardelli with illusions by Jim Steinmeyer — the stage tricks are the point and they are very good. Final week of the run, which closes on 1 November.

events.title: Psychic Standup with Karen Rontowski
events.note: Second night, half past seven.

events.title: Riot Halloween
events.note: Ten o'clock, 21+. The Sunnyvale club's Friday Halloween party, street parking free after six and Caltrain six minutes away.

events.title: Mœnia
events.note: Mexican synth-pop with María José also on the bill — a double header that will fill the Civic with people who know every word.

events.title: Pablo Francisco
events.note: First of four shows across the weekend. Twenty-five years of movie-trailer voices and crowd work. The club lists the run as four shows without splitting the times.

events.title: Filoli Reserve: A Legacy Wine Tasting
events.note: Three sittings — midday, half past one and three — of Chase Cellars wines in the garden. A tasting rather than a listing, included because the setting makes it one.

events.title: Let the Poets Speak: Philip Glass and Allen Ginsberg
events.note: Timo Andres, Taylor Mac and the San Francisco Girls Chorus on the Glass–Ginsberg collaboration — Hydrogen Jukebox and the rest. Half past seven in Bing, and the most interesting programme on the Peninsula this week.

events.title: Blues Traveler
events.note: The second night, no support. Caltrain Menlo Park is four minutes' walk, which genuinely beats driving here.

events.title: Gutenberg! The Musical!
events.note: Two men pitch a terrible musical about the inventor of movable type, playing every part with a hat. Hillbarn's run closes on 1 November.

events.title: Nightfall at Filoli
events.note: The estate's Halloween walk-through: lit gardens, projections and a house that does not need much help after dark. Final weekend — it closes on 1 November.

events.title: The Addams Family
events.note: Opening night. Palo Alto Players open the musical in the Lucie Stern — the Andrew Lippa score rather than the television theme, and a community company that has been at this since 1931.

events.title: Japanese Tea Garden Free Admission Hour
events.venue: Japanese Tea Garden, Golden Gate Park
events.note: The Friday hour, nine to ten. Free.

events.title: Free Halloween Hike: Presidio Pet Cemetery
events.note: Rafiki Coalition lead a four-hour hike that takes in the Presidio's pet cemetery and the stories attached to it. Free, ten until two.

events.title: Free Quarter-Pound of Candy on Halloween Eve
events.note: Say trick or treat at the Russian Hill counter and leave with a quarter pound, free, eleven until six.

events.title: Pay-What-You-Can Taco Day
events.note: Every Friday, pay from nothing upward. Listed because the brief cares about the things that are easy to miss and this has been running quietly for years.

events.title: City Creatures: Pest Art Pop-Up
events.note: Art about the animals cities call vermin, with guest speakers in the evening. Free open house from two until six, then a ticketed evening.

events.title: Nightmare on Front Street
events.note: A free Halloween block party in the Financial District, two in the afternoon until ten at night. The FiDi does not usually do this and it is worth encouraging.

events.title: Final Weekend of Ocean Beach Bonfires
events.note: The fire rings close for the winter after this weekend. First come, first served from three, free, and bring more wood than you think you need.

events.title: Free Outdoor Video Art Walk: Meet the Moment
events.note: The Meet the Moment video festival puts work on screens and façades along a Mid-Market loop, four until nine, three nights running. Free, no RSVP, and a genuinely good use of that stretch of Market.

events.title: Hayes Valley Glowing Trick-or-Treat Trail
events.note: Shopfronts along Hayes hand out sweets from four, and there is a free outdoor film at the end of it. Free, six hours, and the best-run of the neighbourhood trails.

events.title: The Moors
events.note: Friday's four o'clock performance of the Silverman.

events.title: Battle of the Decades DJ Party
events.note: Free admission with RSVP, $1 drinks, North Beach. Decade-versus-decade pop.

events.title: Free Outdoor Movie Night: Despicable Me 4
events.note: Free film, free food and free popcorn in the Parkside, five-thirty until eight. Bring a blanket; it is the Sunset in October.

events.title: Crawloween 2026
events.note: The city's 25,000-strong Halloween pub crawl, running from the 24th to the 1st. $15 with the discount code. Enormous, and not for everyone.

events.title: Fjord
events.note: Cristian Mungiu's new film: a Norwegian woman and her devout Romanian husband move their five children to a remote coastal community. From the Palme d'Or winner for 4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days.

events.title: NAZA
events.note: Early evening screening.

events.title: New People: My Undesirable Friends: Part 2 – Exile (Chapters 1–3)
events.note: Julia Loktev's long-form documentary on independent Russian journalists, with a recorded introduction by executive producer Meryl Streep. Three chapters in one sitting.

events.title: Cold Cave and SRSQ
events.note: Substance Festival night two, and the stronger bill: Wesley Eisold solo, plus Kennedy Ashlyn's SRSQ, whose voice is the best instrument in this scene. Houses of Heaven and False Figure open.

events.title: SF Halloween BOOs Cruise
events.note: Ninety minutes on the bay in costume, $50 adult. The bridge at night is the selling point and the DJ is incidental.

events.title: Floating Features: Us
events.note: Jordan Peele's doppelgänger film, set partly in Santa Cruz — a local-geography horror screening the night before Halloween.

events.title: Golden Gate Comedy Night
events.note: Free with RSVP, 21+. Comics who would normally be at the Punch Line, in a smaller room.

events.title: HellaSecret Crazy Funny Asians
events.note: Two shows, seven and nine, free with RSVP, address on confirmation.

events.title: Rush Hour Comedy Night
events.note: The Function's Black and Asian comedians' showcase, free with RSVP.

events.title: Manon
events.note: Penultimate performance.

events.title: SF Symphony: Elim Chan conducts Adams, Mendelssohn and Brahms
events.note: Second of three. Orchestra seats were still listed from $59 when this was compiled, which for a programme this good is the bargain of the week.

events.title: An Evening With Montell Fish
events.note: Bedroom gospel-soul that has quietly built an enormous audience; the Nest tour is the first time he has played rooms this size here. Lower-register, slow, and very still.

events.title: Lime Garden
events.note: Brighton four-piece playing wiry, danceable indie with the rhythm section well up in the mix. Sold out, with a waitlist; Whalefall support.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Mischief's hijacking of Peter Pan, in which an am-dram company's flying rig fails in every way a flying rig can. Broad, exactly timed, and the best-engineered farce in the city.

events.title: Stella Lefty
events.note: Sold out. Country-leaning pop songwriter on the Lefty Live bill, with Grace Enger. All ages, which is unusual here.

events.title: The Batcave SF: Dance Party and Drag Show
events.note: Goth night with drag, named for the London club that invented the genre. 21+.

events.title: The Confessional
events.note: Audience secrets, read out and then improvised. Endgames run three shows most Fridays and this is the one that goes wrong best.

events.title: The Stoner Comedy Jam
events.note: Stand-up in a consumption lounge, free with RSVP, 21+. The premise is self-explanatory and it works.

events.title: Word for Word: Assimilation
events.note: Word for Word stage E.L. Doctorow's Assimilation and Tatyana Tolstaya's story word for word, stage directions included — a green-card marriage that turns real. The company's method is the draw: nothing is adapted away.

events.title: A Night of the Living Dead
events.note: folkYEAH!'s Halloween jam summit: Lebo, Holly Bowling, Wally Ingram, Elliott Peck and Danny Luehring improvising on Grateful Dead material. Long sets, loose structure.

events.title: Temptation, Dead Souls and Flippy Floppy
events.note: A post-punk tribute triple: New Order, Joy Division and Talking Heads, in that order of billing. Tribute acts, so the brief says list them and never feature them — but this is a well-chosen lineage. 21+.

events.title: Coral 9, Bazooka, Dogwater and DJ Kalamansi
events.note: Four local acts and a DJ, nine o'clock. The sort of bill this room puts on better than anyone — nobody on it is touring. $25.50, all ages.

events.title: High Step Society
events.note: Electro-swing with a live horn section — more fun than the genre name suggests, and a reliable dance-floor booking. HABITAAT supports.

events.title: Italoween with Club Giovanni
events.note: Italo-disco all night from the Club Giovanni DJs. The most specific genre commitment of the Halloween weekend.

events.title: The Infinite Wrench
events.note: Thirty plays in sixty minutes, order decided by the audience shouting numbers, the menu replaced every week. $13 plus the roll of a die at the door — the cheapest live theatre in the city and the only one where the price is random.

events.title: Wonkywilla
events.note: Bass and UK garage, doors at 9.

events.title: Your Fucked Up Relationship
events.note: Same company, later slot, same method applied to break-ups.

events.title: Alien
events.note: Opens tonight and runs into November. Ridley Scott's 1979 film in a 230-seat room is the version it was built for.

events.title: Haus Party Halloween
events.note: The room's long-running house and disco night, in costume. Cheapest door of the Halloween weekend at $8.15 advance. 21+.

events.title: The Ritual
events.note: The 10:15 show, once a week and the loosest of the three.

events.title: BATS Improv
events.note: Long-form improv in the Bayfront Theater at Fort Mason, Fridays and Saturdays through the end of the year. The company has been doing this on this pier since 1986.

events.title: FRNDS Only Halloween
events.note: The club's own Halloween party across its rooms. Costume, 21+, and no announced headliner — the booking is the building.

events.title: Galactic
events.note: First of two. The New Orleans funk band now own Tipitina's, which tells you how seriously they take the lineage. Bella Rayne opens.

events.title: Hell in a Bucket
events.note: Grateful Dead DJ night in a Divisadero bar, which is a more San Francisco sentence than it ought to be. Free.

events.title: Holdfast
events.note: Melodic hardcore, with Time Crunch and Cheers to Nothing. Taken from DNA's two mirrors, which agree on this one; the club's own calendar refuses this run by name, so no time is available.

events.title: John Scofield
events.note: Scofield with Larry Goldings on organ, Oteil Burbridge on bass and Adam Deitch on drums — a jam-band rhythm section behind a jazz guitarist, which is exactly the hybrid he has spent forty years refusing to resolve. Start time not published on the mirror this file uses.

events.title: Marshmello
events.note: Arena-scale EDM in a Dogpatch warehouse. Findable without this digest and listed for completeness.

events.title: Monolink and The Blaze
events.note: Live electronic with guitars, plus the French duo whose videos are better than their sets. mindchatter opens.

events.title: Movies at Mechanics'
events.note: The Friday-evening film series in the 1854 library's fourth-floor meeting room, 57 Post Street. Downtown SF's page for the series carries the dates but not the title, and both it and the institute's own site refused this run, so the programme is unconfirmed.

events.title: Oh, Mary!
events.note: Cole Escola's Mary Todd Lincoln as a thwarted cabaret singer, at the Curran rather than an A.C.T. house. A.C.T. publishes no curtain times anywhere on its site, which is the theatre's choice and not a fetch failure — check the ticket page.

events.title: Paper Skies
events.note: Second stage on the Lost In Dreams Friday. Melodic bass.

events.title: Parra for Cuva
events.note: Nicolas Demuth's downtempo electronic project, built from acoustic samples and sung fragments. Closer to a concert than a DJ set.

events.title: Party 4 U
events.note: Hyperpop and 2010s club edits, free in. The pre-Halloween option for people who do not want a $40 ticket.

events.title: SET Halloween with Lost Miracle
events.note: Sébastien Léger and Roy Rosenfeld as Lost Miracle, with Satori SF — melodic, long-form house on a Funktion-One rig. The costume end of techno rather than the costume end of pop.

events.title: The Chicks
events.note: The second of two. See Thursday.

events.title: The Haunt
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: Night two of three. See Thursday.

events.title: Trunk or Treat at the Lake
events.note: Boot-to-boot sweets at the Edoff Memorial Bandstand, eleven until two, free.

events.title: Free Oakland Up Market
events.note: Everything outdoors is free to take, Friday to Sunday, midday until four. A genuine free store and not a metaphor.

events.title: Oakland Chinatown Trick or Treat Trail
events.note: The Chinatown trail starts in the cultural centre lobby, two until four, free.

events.title: La maison des bois: Episodes 4–7
events.note: Maurice Pialat's 1971 television series, four episodes in an afternoon sitting. Half past two — a long, quiet, extremely good way to spend a Friday.

events.title: HellaSecret Speakeasy Comedy
events.note: Friday pop-up, address on RSVP, limited free tickets.

events.title: Sci-Fi Night: Little Shop of Horrors
events.note: The film, plus actual carnivorous plants to look at, in the hills observatory. $20 for over-18s, $10 for members. The pairing is the joke and the botany is real.

events.title: A Woman Is a Woman
events.note: Godard's 1961 colour musical-that-is-not-a-musical, in the early-films series whose posters by Gvido Augusts are hung upstairs. Half past seven.

events.title: Burndown Tour 2026
events.note: Febuary, Love Letter, Stella and more, half past seven, five dollars. All ages.

events.title: Shpongle
events.note: First of two nights of Simon Posford's psychedelic dub, with Mindex and Cosmic Trigger, visuals by Jonathan Singer and Glass Crane, and live floral art by Anthony Ward. Entirely sincere and all the better for it.

events.title: Hell Comes to Oakland IV
events.note: Night one of two. The Stork's own Halloween punk festival, fourth year. $13–$22, 21+.

events.title: Liberation
events.note: Friday. Curtain time unconfirmed.

events.title: Oakland Ballet: Luna Mexicana
events.note: The company's Día de los Muertos programme, now a fixture — folklórico and ballet together, with mariachi, in a 1931 art deco house. Tickets needed for everyone over two.

events.title: Richie Hawtin and Boys Noize
events.note: An aircraft hangar at the old naval air station, with Indira Paganotto, 999999999, Salome and more. Hawtin has been doing this since 1990 and the room suits him.

events.title: Rick Braun
events.note: Trumpet and flugelhorn at the smooth-jazz end of the room's booking. $39–$84; start time was not listed on the venue's calendar.

events.title: Surprise Chef
events.note: Melbourne's cinematic-soul instrumentalists, with Tommy Guerrero — the skater turned guitarist whose records are better than anyone expects. Orinda is not on the brief's region list; filed east-bay by proximity.

events.title: Bluey's Big Play
events.venue: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Ten in the morning on Halloween.

events.title: Cute Ridge Halloween Market
events.note: A free Halloween edition of the Y2K-and-trinkets market, ten until six. Free candy, free entry, and a mall, which is honest about what it is.

events.title: Sunnyvale Autumn Food Festival
events.note: Two days of food stalls in downtown Sunnyvale, ten until five, free to walk in. A genuine festival rather than a restaurant promotion, which is the test the brief sets.

events.title: Sharks vs Senators
events.note: A one o'clock Halloween afternoon face-off, billed as Los Tiburones. Early enough to do something else afterwards, which is the selling point.

events.title: Bluey's Big Play
events.venue: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Two o'clock Saturday.

events.title: Dracula
events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Halloween matinee. Steven Dietz's adaptation of Stoker, directed by Giovanna Sardelli with illusions by Jim Steinmeyer — the stage tricks are the point and they are very good. Final week of the run, which closes on 1 November.

events.title: Dracula
events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Halloween night, half past seven — the right date for it, and it will sell. Steven Dietz's adaptation of Stoker, directed by Giovanna Sardelli with illusions by Jim Steinmeyer — the stage tricks are the point and they are very good. Final week of the run, which closes on 1 November.

events.title: Halloween Costume Party
events.note: Nine o'clock, no announced lineup. This is not on Live Nation's page for the venue or on the Songkick mirror — it comes off a nightlife listing app, so treat it as unconfirmed.

events.title: Halloween Massive with YG
events.note: YG in a Sunnyvale nightclub on Halloween, ten o'clock, 21+ — the same night he is billed at a SoMa warehouse, so one of the two may move.

events.title: Jorge Medina
events.note: The former La Arrolladora singer, solo, on Halloween night. Banda, and the Civic's third Spanish-language sell-out of the week.

events.title: Pablo Francisco
events.note: Halloween night; the club usually plays two on a Saturday. Times unconfirmed.

events.title: Halloween Trick-or-Treat at the Farmers Market
events.note: Eight until noon at the Gilman Street market, free, children in costume. The earliest start in the digest.

events.title: Free Halloween Night at the Museum and Flashlight Ghost Hunt
events.note: The Museum of American Heritage opens after dark for a flashlight hunt through its collection of early technology. Free with RSVP, five until nine, and the best free Halloween thing on the Peninsula.

events.title: Haunted Halloween with Stu Allen & Mars Hotel
events.note: Grateful Dead repertoire played by the best of the Bay Area's many such bands, in costume. A tribute act, so listed and not featured, but it is the Peninsula's Halloween night.

events.title: Autumn Days at Filoli
events.note: The daytime version: giant pumpkins, cider and churros across the formal gardens. Closes 1 November.

events.title: Foreverland and Starman SF
events.note: Michael Jackson and Bowie tributes on a double bill with a liquid light show, Halloween night at the Fox. Tributes, so listed and not featured; the light show is the draw.

events.title: Gutenberg! The Musical!
events.note: Two men pitch a terrible musical about the inventor of movable type, playing every part with a hat. Hillbarn's run closes on 1 November.

events.title: Knocked Loose and Denzel Curry
events.note: The Kentucky hardcore band and the Florida rapper on one bill, with Superheaven and Boundaries. In the Cow Palace's warehouse rather than the arena, which is the better room.

events.title: Knocked Loose and Denzel Curry
events.note: Filed again here for the Peninsula: the Palace Warehouse rather than the arena floor, with Superheaven and Boundaries. Daly City is on the brief's Peninsula list.

events.title: Nightfall at Filoli
events.note: Halloween night on the estate. Parking is $10 on the grounds lot and the walk is long; wear boots.

events.title: The Addams Family
events.note: Halloween night, which is either obvious or perfect. Palo Alto Players open the musical in the Lucie Stern — the Andrew Lippa score rather than the television theme, and a community company that has been at this since 1931.

events.title: Free Legion of Honor Museum Day for Bay Area Residents
events.note: Same museum group, same free Saturday, same ID. The Lincoln Park site and the view from the colonnade are half the reason to go.

events.title: Free de Young Museum Day for Bay Area Residents
events.venue: de Young Museum, Golden Gate Park
events.note: Every Saturday the de Young is free to Bay Area residents with ID, half past nine until a quarter past five. On Halloween with the park full, take Muni.

events.title: Free Labyrinth Screening
events.note: Jim Henson's 1986 film free at the ten o'clock show only — later showings are ticketed. The puppets hold up better than the effects.

events.title: Halloween SF World Naked Bike Ride
events.note: Costume optional and so is everything else. Meets at Rincon Park, free, and genuinely one of the things this digest exists to tell you about.

events.title: Halloween Storytime in Francisco Park
events.note: Forty-five minutes of stories in the new Russian Hill park, free, half past ten.

events.title: 12th Annual Chinatown Halloween Festival
events.note: Waverly Place closed off for a free block party, eleven until three. Twelve years in and still the best-scaled Halloween event in the city for children.

events.title: North Beach Cleanup with Free Lunch
events.note: Ninety minutes of litter-picking on Green Street and lunch afterwards. Free, register on Civic Joy.

events.title: SF Cake Picnic Fall 2026
events.note: Hundreds of home-baked cakes on trestle tables, tasted by ticket. $57.50, which is a lot, and it sells out anyway.

events.title: Wags & Wheels Halloween Dog Pawty
events.note: Trunk-or-treat for dogs beside a classic car show at the Wharf, eleven until three. Free to attend.

events.title: Word for Wordplay: Spooky Fam Jam
events.note: Eleven in the morning on Halloween: a handful of spooky, family-safe tales told by the Word for Word company. An hour, and the only children's theatre in the Mission this week.

events.title: Séance
events.note: Director Vivian Kerr in attendance. An 1892 California woman takes refuge from a storm and from her own adultery; a first feature, and the Q&A is the draw.

events.title: Craft & Learn at the Museum of the Eye: Ojo de Dios
events.note: Make a God's-eye yarn weaving in the ophthalmology museum, free with RSVP. The museum is small, free and far stranger than its name.

events.title: Crawloween 2026
events.note: Halloween-night leg of the citywide crawl, two in the afternoon until ten.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Halloween matinee, and the family-friendly option. Mischief's hijacking of Peter Pan, in which an am-dram company's flying rig fails in every way a flying rig can. Broad, exactly timed, and the best-engineered farce in the city.

events.title: The Red Shoes
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: Powell and Pressburger's 1948 film, in a weekly series on voyeurism and theatricality chosen alongside GaHee Park's paintings. $15 includes themed snacks and gallery entry.

events.title: The Witches
events.note: Roxie Kids. Nicolas Roeg's 1990 Roald Dahl adaptation with Anjelica Huston, which traumatised a generation and is much better than the remake.

events.title: Dance Thrill Fest VI
events.note: REYES Dance's sixth annual dance-film festival — short works where choreography is made for the camera rather than filmed from a seat. Nothing else in the week does this.

events.title: Free Outdoor Video Art Walk: Meet the Moment
events.note: Night two of the Mid-Market video loop, free, four until nine.

events.title: New People: The Snake Girl and the Silver-Haired Witch
events.note: Noriaki Yuasa's 1968 Daiei horror for children, from the Gamera director. Genuinely eerie and only 82 minutes.

events.title: Ocular Oddities: 21+ After Hours
events.note: The eye museum after dark with a drink in your hand, $20.72. Glass eyes, Civil War surgical kits, and an octopus's point of view.

events.title: Lady
events.note: Late-afternoon show.

events.title: Fjord
events.note: Second night of the Mungiu.

events.title: SF Halloween Night BOOs Cruise
events.note: The Halloween-night sailing, ninety minutes, $50 adult.

events.title: Crazy Funny Asians
events.note: Free showcase, RSVP required.

events.title: Golden Gate Comedy Night
events.note: Halloween-night free comedy, RSVP, 21+.

events.title: SF Symphony: Elim Chan conducts Adams, Mendelssohn and Brahms
events.note: The last of three, on Halloween night. Doctor Atomic Symphony after the interval is an unsettling piece of programming for the date and almost certainly deliberate.

events.title: The Marriage of Figaro
events.note: Opening night of the Mozart, on Halloween. A company that can field this and Manon in the same building on the same weekend is in good health.

events.title: Bad Acid Presents: Hallorager XIII
events.note: Thirteenth year of the Mission's garage-punk Halloween rager. Lineup is the promoter's business and tends to be announced late.

events.title: Cobb's Free Comedy Night
events.note: A ghostly, ghastly gameshow, free with RSVP if you arrive thirty minutes early. Chain-venue comedy, ranked low by the brief and free, which earns it a line.

events.title: DJ Mandy Presents: The Raveyard
events.note: Halloween night in the Castro's restored movie palace, turned into a rave. The building is the draw; the Wurlitzer stays shut.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Halloween evening. Mischief's hijacking of Peter Pan, in which an am-dram company's flying rig fails in every way a flying rig can. Broad, exactly timed, and the best-engineered farce in the city.

events.title: Puff Puff Laugh
events.note: Stand-up in the lounge, free with RSVP, 21+.

events.title: The Confessional
events.note: Halloween night's eight o'clock show.

events.title: The Paul Simon Halloween Ball
events.note: Bone Diggers play Graceland and Rhythm of the Saints with Reed Mathis, Lebo and Holly Bowling, on the Chapel's outdoor stage with Mad Alchemy's liquid lights. Dress warm — it is outside.

events.title: Under the Covers 13: A Nightmare on Mission Street
events.note: One night, no originals, thirteenth year. Local bands each take on another band's catalogue for a set. The best-value Halloween ticket in the Mission; DICE lists it twice and it is one show.

events.title: Word for Word: Assimilation
events.note: Word for Word stage E.L. Doctorow's Assimilation and Tatyana Tolstaya's story word for word, stage directions included — a green-card marriage that turns real. The company's method is the draw: nothing is adapted away.

events.title: Emo Nite Halloween
events.note: The LA-born DJ night's Halloween edition. Second emo-themed Halloween party in the city this weekend — the other is at The Independent — and this is the smaller, sweatier one. 21+.

events.title: Gasolina Reggaetón Halloween Party
events.note: The long-running perreo night takes the hall for Halloween. Early-2000s reggaetón and dembow, costumes expected, and the cheapest ticket in the building this week.

events.title: HellaSecret Desi Comedy Night
events.note: Two shows, seven and nine; free for the first hundred RSVPs.

events.title: HydeFM Halloween: The Equation
events.note: AceMo and Swami Sound, which is a genuinely strong pairing — New York house raised on jungle, and the dub-garage producer who followed him. Doors 9.

events.title: Improvement Movement and Adron
events.note: Adron is the reason: Atlanta's Adrienne McCann writes Brazilian-inflected guitar pop in close harmony with herself, and almost nobody books her out here. Nine o'clock, $28.08, all ages.

events.title: The Emo Night Tour
events.note: A DJ night of 2000s emo and pop-punk, in costume. Not a band, and it does not pretend to be; it fills the room every time.

events.title: The Infinite Wrench
events.note: Saturday's run, Halloween night. See Friday.

events.title: Your Fucked Up Relationship
events.note: Nine o'clock, Halloween.

events.title: Wild at Heart (4K Restoration)
events.note: Lynch's 1990 Palme d'Or winner, restored, on Halloween night, and come dressed as a character for free popcorn. Snakeskin jackets encouraged.

events.title: The Mummies
events.note: San Mateo's budget-rock originals, in mummy bandages, playing the most primitive garage punk in California since 1988. Balzac do Prince Buster ska; Big Nate DJs. The Halloween show in the city for anyone over forty. 21+.

events.title: Autograf
events.note: Melodic house, Halloween night.

events.title: BATS Improv
events.note: Saturday night at the Bayfront Theater.

events.title: Big Wild
events.note: Under the 1915 rotunda, with Vandelux and — the real reason to go — Hercules & Love Affair, whose disco is a decade past its moment and has aged well.

events.title: Christian Löffler
events.note: The German producer's melancholy, sample-built house, live. Almas and Paris support. A quieter Halloween than the room's usual and much the better for it.

events.title: Eric Prydz
events.note: A warehouse on Mission Rock, with Tiga and Kelly Lee Owens. The largest-capacity electronic booking of Halloween night in the city.

events.title: Ernest Aines
events.note: A chamber-scale recital in the O'Farrell Street church. The artist plays three Bay Area churches this week, which is its own kind of tour.

events.title: Every Saturday Night (A.C.T. ACTivate)
events.note: Extended to 7 November. A journey into the Fillmore District, from the present back through the echoes of a once-thriving Black neighbourhood. A.C.T. publishes no curtain times anywhere on its site, which is the theatre's choice and not a fetch failure.

events.title: FOR-SITE: Attentive Earth
events.note: Muzae Sesay and Alexcia Sundra in the Guardhouse, through January. FOR-SITE's Fort Mason room is small and consistently the best free gallery on the waterfront.

events.title: Freak-O-Ween 2026
events.note: The Treasures, Bolero and The Spiral Electric in the old Mabuhay Gardens room on Broadway — three psych-leaning local bands in a building with more history than its current name.

events.title: Galactic
events.note: Halloween night, with Parlor Greens — a Hammond-organ trio who are the best support booking on the bill all week.

events.title: Haines Gallery: 250 Years, Indigenous Futures
events.note: Haines Gallery's answer to the semiquincentennial, hung at Fort Mason and running to 7 November. Free.

events.title: Introducing The Aces
events.note: Provo four-piece — all queer, all playing their own instruments, writing bright guitar-pop about it. Gatlin opens. A Halloween show that is actually a gig.

events.title: John Scofield
events.note: Night two of three, same quartet. Time unconfirmed — the mirror does not carry it.

events.title: MFHD
events.note: Stand-up on Halloween night at the Punch Line. Chain-venue comedy, which the brief ranks low — listed for completeness.

events.title: Medium Build
events.note: Nick Carpenter's Anchorage-raised project — big, hoarse, confessional rock songs that have outgrown clubs very fast. The Scratch also on the bill.

events.title: Oh, Mary!
events.note: Cole Escola's Mary Todd Lincoln as a thwarted cabaret singer, at the Curran rather than an A.C.T. house. A.C.T. publishes no curtain times anywhere on its site, which is the theatre's choice and not a fetch failure — check the ticket page.

events.title: RL Grime
events.note: The Halloween trap institution, with NGHTMRE and a dozen more across the Lost In Dreams bill — Silcrow, Nitepunk, IMANU, WINK and others. The biggest electronic lineup of the week by count.

events.title: Rudy Can't Fail
events.note: Two-tone and ska 45s, named for the Clash song. Runs alongside the dance jam.

events.title: Sacha Robotti
events.note: Tech-house in a small SoMa room. 21+.

events.title: Scaling Intelligence
events.note: On view, free, during gallery hours — the exhibition closes on 1 November, so this is the last Saturday for it. Hours are not published on the page; check before crossing town.

events.title: Sistek
events.note: Progressive house, Halloween night at Audio. 21+.

events.title: The Haunt
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: Halloween night, the last of three.

events.title: The No Theme Super Spooky Dance Jam
events.note: Halloween night, no stated genre, no cover before the late hour. The bar's own party rather than a promoter's.

events.title: The Schisms, Neurotrash, Northern Waste and Unko Atama
events.note: Four-band Halloween punk bill in the upstairs room. Unko Atama are the draw — Osaka hardcore, rarely here.

events.title: YG and Mozzy
events.note: With KALAN.FRFR, Natalie Nunn and Chef Boy. A SoMa warehouse Halloween show; the Mozzy billing is the Bay interest.

events.title: ZHU
events.note: The first of two ZHU bookings in the city the same night — this one and Space 550 — which is either ambitious or a listings error. Treat the pair as unconfirmed.

events.title: Spooky Science at Chabot
events.note: Halloween-day programming for families at the science centre, from ten. $24.

events.title: Performance: Entanglement
events.note: Steffani Jemison and Leslie Cuyjet respond to Maren Hassinger and Senga Nengudi in the galleries, one o'clock. An hour, and it will not be repeated.

events.title: Paramount Movie Classics: Frankenstein
events.note: James Whale's 1931 film at three in the afternoon on Halloween, in the deco palace, with the Wurlitzer and a newsreel first. Cheap and perfect.

events.title: Vivre sa vie
events.note: Anna Karina in twelve tableaux, four o'clock. The best of the early Godards and the saddest.

events.title: Kwaidan
events.note: Masaki Kobayashi's 1964 anthology of Japanese ghost stories, half past six on Halloween, in a room with a proper screen. Three hours and the most beautiful horror film ever shot.

events.title: Oakland Comedy Saturday Night
events.note: Two shows, seven and nine, free with code. Halloween night.

events.title: Spy, Fentanyl, No Guard, Violent Imagery and Rose Chamber
events.note: Halloween at Gilman: five hardcore bands for five dollars, seven o'clock, all ages, no bar. The best-value ticket of the night anywhere in the Bay Area.

events.title: House of Velvet: Halloween
events.note: Juju's Productions' burlesque and variety night takes the room on Halloween. 18+, $45–$65.

events.title: Shpongle
events.note: Halloween night, with Supersillyus instead of Mindex. The Fox's plaster interior is the right building for this.

events.title: The Rocky Horror Picture Show
events.note: Halloween night, $16.50 all in, with the usual participation. The cheapest Halloween ticket in the East Bay and the only one with a script.

events.title: Hell Comes to Oakland IV
events.note: Night two, nine o'clock, billed as the tribute night. $13–$22, 21+.

events.title: CelloGayageum
events.note: A cello and a Korean gayageum, playing each other's repertoire — the kind of booking the Freight does better than anywhere else in the region. Time not listed on the mirror.

events.title: DJ K
events.note: Halloween on the 19th Street rooftop. Downtown Oakland garages shut their gates at seven on weekdays — BART is the answer here.

events.title: J. Jaxx
events.note: Halloween night in the Uptown bar.

events.title: Liberation
events.note: Saturday. Curtain time unconfirmed; Berkeley Rep usually plays a matinee and an evening on Saturdays.

events.title: Stanley Simmons
events.note: Halloween night. He plays Felton Music Hall the following night, which is consistent with a real routing; Cornerstone's own calendar still does not list it.

events.title: Tyga
events.note: Halloween night at the arena. Listed for completeness.

events.title: Bluey's Big Play
events.venue: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Ten in the morning.

events.title: Sunnyvale Autumn Food Festival
events.note: Day two, ten until five, free.

events.title: Dracula
events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Closing matinee at one o'clock. Steven Dietz's adaptation of Stoker, directed by Giovanna Sardelli with illusions by Jim Steinmeyer — the stage tricks are the point and they are very good. Final week of the run, which closes on 1 November.

events.title: Bluey's Big Play
events.venue: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: The closing two o'clock performance.

events.title: Katsura Sunshine's Rakugo
events.note: A Canadian who trained as a rakugo storyteller in Japan — four-hundred-year-old comic monologues, performed kneeling, in English. Four o'clock show; there is a seven o'clock as well.

events.title: Katsura Sunshine's Rakugo
events.note: The seven o'clock performance.

events.title: Pablo Francisco
events.note: The last of the run. Time unconfirmed.

events.title: San Jose Barracuda vs Bakersfield Condors
events.note: First of three against Bakersfield. The brief likes minor-league sport and this is the cheapest live sport in the South Bay.

events.title: Oceánica Ballet 2026
events.note: A family ballet programme with tickets from $19 for the one o'clock. Community-scale and cheap.

events.title: The Psychedelic Furs
events.note: Richard Butler's voice has not softened, and the band have been playing better in the last decade than they did in the 1990s. We Are Scientists support, four days after their own Rickshaw Stop headline. The Peninsula booking of the week.

events.title: Autumn Days at Filoli
events.note: The last day of Autumn Days.

events.title: Gutenberg! The Musical!
events.note: Closing performance. Two men pitch a terrible musical about the inventor of movable type, playing every part with a hat. Hillbarn's run closes on 1 November.

events.title: Kapo: Afro Rosa Tour
events.note: The Colombian singer's Afrobeats-and-champeta hybrid, which has been very big at home and barely tours here.

events.title: Nightfall at Filoli
events.note: The last night of Nightfall for 2026.

events.title: The Addams Family
events.note: Sunday, most likely a matinee — Palo Alto Players publish their times only on the ticketing page. Palo Alto Players open the musical in the Lucie Stern — the Andrew Lippa score rather than the television theme, and a community company that has been at this since 1931.

events.title: 5th Annual Día de los Muertos and Market in the Sunset
events.note: Ofrenda, makers and food on Irving Street, free, nine until two. The Outer Sunset's own Day of the Dead rather than the Mission's.

events.title: Lower Nob Hill Weekly Cleanup
events.note: An hour and a quarter of street cleaning and lunch after. Free.

events.title: Asian Art Museum Free Admission Day
events.note: Free every first Sunday; special exhibitions may still charge. Ten until five.

events.title: Free Labyrinth Screening
events.note: The second free ten o'clock Labyrinth of the weekend.

events.title: Castro Art Mart
events.note: First-Sunday mini block party on Noe Street — LGBTQ artists selling work, live music and drag, free, eleven until five.

events.title: Head West Marketplace at the Ferry Building
events.note: The roving makers' market's first-Sunday slot on the Embarcadero. Free, eleven until four.

events.title: Lindy in the Park
events.note: Thirty-plus years of free Sunday swing dancing on JFK Drive, eleven until two, rain cancels. Beginners taught at the start.

events.title: Aquarium of the Bay: Underwater Pumpkin Carving
events.note: Divers carve pumpkins in the tanks while the fish investigate. $29, and children under twelve in costume go free.

events.title: Golden Gate Park Sunday Roller Disco
events.note: Skatin' Place, one until five, free, sound system supplied by whoever turns up with it. One of the great San Francisco institutions and entirely unofficial.

events.title: Halloween Cookie Picnic
events.note: The overflow event for the sold-out cake picnic, one until three. $57.50.

events.title: The Koffs, Poor Luckies and Drugs
events.note: A one o'clock Sunday matinee — three bands before the afternoon is out, which is the civilised way to do this.

events.title: Crawloween 2026: Día de los Muertos
events.note: The crawl's final day, themed for the date, two until ten.

events.title: Manon
events.note: Closing matinee, and the last chance this season.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Sunday matinee. Mischief's hijacking of Peter Pan, in which an am-dram company's flying rig fails in every way a flying rig can. Broad, exactly timed, and the best-engineered farce in the city.

events.title: Sundays at the Beach Chair Yoga
events.note: Free chair yoga on the closed Great Highway, two o'clock. The promenade's programming is still finding its feet and this is part of it.

events.title: Tenderloin Street Fair: Día de Muertos
events.note: A free Día de Muertos street fair and block party in the Tenderloin, two until eight. Six hours, free, and the neighbourhood's own.

events.title: Word for Word: Assimilation
