events.note: Sunday matinee. Word for Word stage E.L. Doctorow's Assimilation and Tatyana Tolstaya's story word for word, stage directions included — a green-card marriage that turns real. The company's method is the draw: nothing is adapted away.

events.title: SF Latino Film Festival: Strawberry Lips
events.note: The Cine+Más queer film showcase. Half past two.

events.title: SF Civic Music Free Concert
events.note: The San Francisco Civic Music Association's free afternoon concert — amateur orchestral players, donations accepted, RSVP.

events.title: Free Outdoor Video Art Walk: Meet the Moment
events.note: The last of three nights on the Mid-Market loop. Free, four until nine.

events.title: Sad Girl Presents Pope Suburban
events.note: Sunday matinee: Pope Suburban from Los Angeles with Deadramones, Tree Eater and Rat Fuck. Four bands from five o'clock.

events.title: Cobb's Comedy Showcase
events.note: Free with RSVP, arrive thirty minutes early.

events.title: Free Sunday Comedy Night
events.note: Free with Eventbrite RSVP, seven until ten.

events.title: Funky Folk Night
events.note: Acorn & Company and Northern Disconnection, Sunday evening. Acoustic and loose.

events.title: Cardinal Bloom and The Gontiks
events.note: Sunday eight o'clock, all ages. Shoegaze-adjacent locals.

events.title: Frankie and The Witch Fingers
events.note: Psyched! Fest closes with its loudest act — motorik garage-psych played at punk tempo. Carrion Kids and Starzdust open.

events.title: Reggae Sunday
events.note: The standing Sunday-night dance, roots and rocksteady on vinyl.

events.title: SIX60
events.note: New Zealand's biggest band by a distance — stadium-filling at home, playing a 500-cap room here. Soul-pop with reggae in the rhythm section. Cilantro opens solo.

events.title: Token
events.note: Massachusetts rapper built on breath control and density — technical to a fault, and a long way from the room's usual indie booking. Clark D and Delivery Boys open.

events.title: 55CASTLES and Ominess
events.note: With In Shame and The Gallery. Again from the mirrors only — the two disagree on the billing order, and neither carries a start time.

events.title: Baby Smoove Live!
events.note: Detroit's deadpan rapper on the Purple Heart tour — all punchlines, no hooks, delivered like he is bored of being funny.

events.title: Dani Flow
events.note: The Mexican rapper's blunt, very funny reggaetón, in a small Valencia Street room.

events.title: John Scofield
events.note: The last of three. Time unconfirmed.

events.title: José Madero
events.note: The former Panda frontman, now writing solo in Spanish with the guitars still up. Wonderfox support.

events.title: New People: The Gymnasts of Fisherman Colony
events.note: Documentary at New People Cinema. Time not published on the week view when read — confirm before setting out.

events.title: Oh, Mary!
events.note: Closing performance of the run, which ends 1 November. Cole Escola's Mary Todd Lincoln as a thwarted cabaret singer, at the Curran rather than an A.C.T. house. A.C.T. publishes no curtain times anywhere on its site, which is the theatre's choice and not a fetch failure — check the ticket page.

events.title: THX 1138 (35mm)
events.note: George Lucas's first feature on 35mm. Start time was not published on the Roxie's week view when read; confirm before setting out.

events.title: The Musical Box
events.note: The Montreal outfit who reproduce 1970s Genesis staging down to the costumes. A tribute act, so listed and not featured — but the only way left to see the Lamb Lies Down staged.

events.title: Tom Jones
events.note: Eighty-six years old and still touring; the voice has dropped and roughened into something closer to the blues records he always wanted to make. A legacy booking that earns the word.

events.title: Undying, Deliria and 13 Thrones
events.note: Death metal in the Richmond, with Broken Glass Sanctuary. A Sunday bill, which tells you something about the scene's work ethic.

events.title: Black Spaces: Reclaim & Remain
events.note: Displacement, resistance and resilience in Black Oakland, braided together. Free on the first Sunday.

events.title: Free First Sunday at OMCA
events.note: Free admission all day on the first Sunday, eleven until five; the garden and the history and art wings all open. A $6 fee applies to some special exhibitions.

events.title: Radical Blooms: The Unexpected Power of Flowers
events.note: On view on the free Sunday: the museum draws across its own collection to argue that flowers have been doing political work all along. Better than that sounds.

events.title: Students on Strike
events.note: A new installation in the Gallery of California History on the student strikes. Free on the first Sunday.

events.title: Día de Muertos Fiesta with Cumbia DJs
events.note: Free, all ages, midday until nine, with cumbia DJs. Fruitvale's own Day of the Dead, and the biggest free thing in the East Bay this week.

events.title: Free Oakland Up Market
events.note: The Sunday session, midday until four.

events.title: Oakland Ballet: Luna Mexicana
events.note: Sunday matinee, half past two. The best Día de los Muertos ticket in the Bay Area and it is a ballet.

events.title: Cuban Rumba Jam
events.note: Play, sing or dance — an open rumba circle rather than a concert. Free, three o'clock.

events.title: The Valiant Ones
events.note: King Hu's 1975 wuxia, restored. Four o'clock, and the fight choreography is still the standard.

events.title: Día de Muertos Celebración
events.note: Ceremony, ofrenda, son jarocho and food at La Peña, five until nine. Free, donations encouraged. Son jarocho played by people who grew up with it.

events.title: HellaSecret Speakeasy Comedy
events.note: Sunday evening pop-up, free with RSVP.

events.title: GoodFellas
events.note: Seven o'clock. Part of the Scorsese strand running alongside the Hong Kong season.

events.title: Ja Ronn & Flow: That 80s Flow
events.note: Eighties soul and boogie played live rather than DJ'd. $39–$69.

events.title: Worst Party Ever, Equipment, Ogbert The Nerd and Flight Patterns
events.note: Fourth-wave emo on a Sunday, seven o'clock, five dollars.

events.title: La Santa Cecilia
events.note: The Grammy-winning Los Angeles band's cumbia, bolero and rock in Spanish, on a Sunday in Orinda. Filed east-bay by proximity.

events.title: Liberation
events.note: Sunday. Curtain time unconfirmed.

events.title: Pigeons Playing Ping Pong
events.note: Maryland funk-jam quartet, with Dizgo. $35 plus fees. Long sets and a crowd that knows them.

events.title: bunii
events.note: Sunday booking off the sweep. Not on the venue's own calendar.

events.title: Etana
events.note: Two Grammy nominations, a career built on roots reggae sung rather than toasted, and a 300-capacity room in Mill Valley — she does not usually play anything this small in the States. DJ Sep opens. Doors seven. The only outer-region listing this week that clears the brief's bar for the drive, and the Golden Gate toll is southbound only.
